mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as accommodative monetary policy supports equity valuations and economic recovery.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE change and returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) rise and industrial production (INDPRO) falls, it indicates a consumption-driven slowdown with weak supply response, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and falling INDPRO fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term's coefficient is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and sustained), S&P 500 forward returns are negative due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 4.5% and sustained for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered tightening periods, or the average return in tightening cycles is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 500,000 units (annualized) consistently predict positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as strong housing activity signals economic expansion and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST exceeds 500,000 units, or Rank IC is below 0.05 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in non-farm payrolls exceeding 50,000 signals worsening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to immediate economic contraction fears.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the correlation between PAYEMS change and returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes (INDPRO falling below 90 for two consecutive months), S&P 500 forward returns are negative due to reduced economic output and inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered supply shock periods, or the average return in supply shocks is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate falls and unemployment rises simultaneously, it signals a deepening recession, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to heightened economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: The joint signal of falling FEDFUNDS and rising UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term's coefficient is not significant (p > 0.05).
